rationale:
The supplied proof combines three independent obligations, each of a different kind: (i) step 1 (F1), mass subadditivity M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B), a general and reusable fact about Simon's mass (a supremum over admissible forms) that holds for every U and G; (ii) step 2, the triangle inequality for the flat-type closeness relation through a common center Q (current algebra plus (IS) plus F1); (iii) steps 4–5, the nested-infinite-sets diagonal extraction, which is pure combinatorics with no currents involved and is the only recursive construction. Splitting along these lines isolates the measure-theoretic sup argument, the current identities and the recursion into three small, self-contained, reusable lemmas. The only parts left in the parent are step 3 (the pigeonhole) and the arithmetic.

How the children imply the selected statement by the supplied proof: apply diagonal_subseq with C r j l := ∃ IM R, S, X_j − X_l − S = ∂R ∧ M(R) + M(S) ≤ (2⁻¹)^r. Its hypothesis is step 3. Given r and an infinite I ⊆ ℕ, take the parent hypothesis at η := (2⁻¹)^(r+1) > 0 (ENNReal.pow_pos) and choose Q_j ∈ 𝒬, R_j, S_j for every j. Because I ⊆ ⋃_{Q∈𝒬} {j ∈ I | Q_j = Q} and 𝒬 is finite (Set.Finite.biUnion), some fiber J ⊆ I is infinite. For j, l ∈ J (including j = l), Q_j = Q_l = Q, so close_pair gives IM R, S with X_j − X_l − S = ∂R and M(R) + M(S) ≤ (M(R_j)+M(S_j)) + (M(R_l)+M(S_l)) ≤ (2⁻¹)^(r+1) + (2⁻¹)^(r+1) = (2⁻¹)^r (pow_succ, mul_add, ENNReal.inv_two_add_inv_two). The resulting φ is exactly the parent's conclusion. mass_sub_le is consumed inside close_pair, which is a sibling dependency, so the graph is acyclic.

subproblems.title: Mass subadditivity for a difference of currents
subproblems.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ, all sets U, G ⊆ ℝ^P and all currents A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n), M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) in [0, ∞]. Conventions: A − B is the contract instance Sub, so (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω). M_G(X) = X.massOn G is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(X(ω)) over ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n G. These are the test forms ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n: smooth, compactly supported in U) with tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x, called admissible for M_G. Neither U nor G is assumed open.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U G : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), (A - B).massOn G ≤ A.massOn G + B.massOn G
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 (F1) of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_cauchy_subseq (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2).
1. By definition, M_G(A − B) = sSup {ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) : ω ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n G}. By the least-upper-bound property (sSup_le) it suffices to show ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) for every admissible ω. Fix such an ω, so that tsupport ω ⊆ G and covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x.
2. The negative −ω ∈ TestFormOn U n (negation in the submodule) is also admissible for M_G. Its underlying form is x ↦ −ω(x), so tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω ⊆ G (tsupport_neg) and covectorEuclideanNorm(−ω(x)) = covectorEuclideanNorm(ω(x)) ≤ 1 for all x (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
3. By the definition of the contract Sub instance, the linear functional underlying A − B is A.toCurrent − B.toCurrent, so (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) definitionally. Since B is linear, B(−ω) = −B(ω) (LinearMap.map_neg). Hence (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω).
4. For real s, t we have ENNReal.ofReal(s + t) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(s) + ENNReal.ofReal(t) (ENNReal.ofReal_add_le). With step 3 this gives ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(A(ω)) + ENNReal.ofReal(B(−ω)).
5. Since ω is admissible, ENNReal.ofReal(A(ω)) ≤ M_G(A). Since −ω is admissible (step 2), ENNReal.ofReal(B(−ω)) ≤ M_G(B) (GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Adding these bounds (add_le_add) and combining with step 4 gives ENNReal.ofReal((A − B)(ω)) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B) for every admissible ω. By step 1, M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B). ∎
proof_key_steps: Reduce the supremum bound to one admissible form ω (sSup_le).
(A − B)(ω) = A(ω) + B(−ω) by the Sub instance and linearity of B.
ENNReal.ofReal_add_le, then le_massOn for ω (with A) and for −ω (with B).

subproblems.title: Two decompositions with a common center give a close pair
subproblems.statement: Assume (IS): for all P, n ∈ ℕ, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity A, B ∈ 𝒟_n(U), the current A − B is integer multiplicity. Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Let Y, Z, Q, S₁, S₂ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) and R₁, R₂ ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(U), with R₁, S₁, R₂, S₂ integer multiplicity, Y − Q − S₁ = ∂R₁ and Z − Q − S₂ = ∂R₂. Then there are integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(U) and S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) with Y − Z − S = ∂R and M(R) + M(S) ≤ (M(R₁) + M(S₁)) + (M(R₂) + M(S₂)) in [0, ∞]. Conventions: 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d. Subtraction is the contract instance Sub, with (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω). ∂T(ω) = T(dω) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary). M(T) = T.mass = T.massOn U. Integer multiplicity means the contract predicate IsIntegerMultiplicity.
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (A B : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity A → IsIntegerMultiplicity B → IsIntegerMultiplicity (A - B)) → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (Y Z Q S₁ S₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (R₁ R₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 2)), IsOpen U → IsIntegerMultiplicity R₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity S₁ → IsIntegerMultiplicity R₂ → IsIntegerMultiplicity S₂ → Y - Q - S₁ = R₁.boundary → Z - Q - S₂ = R₂.boundary → ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity S ∧ Y - Z - S = R.boundary ∧ R.mass + S.mass ≤ (R₁.mass + S₁.mass) + (R₂.mass + S₂.mass)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 (close pairs) of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_cauchy_subseq (Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2). The mass bound is kept as the sum of the two given masses.
1. Put R := R₁ − R₂ ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(U) and S := S₁ − S₂ ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U) (contract Sub instance). U is open and R₁, R₂ are integer multiplicity, so (IS) with n = m + 2 shows that R is integer multiplicity. Likewise S₁, S₂ are integer multiplicity, so (IS) with n = m + 1 shows that S is integer multiplicity.
2. (Pointwise hypotheses.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+1}(U) (TestFormOn U (m + 1)) and write dω := exteriorDerivativeTestOn U (m + 1) ω ∈ 𝒟^{m+2}(U). Then T.boundary(ω) = T(dω) for every T ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(U), definitionally (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply). Also (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) definitionally for the contract Sub instance. Evaluating the hypotheses Y − Q − S₁ = ∂R₁ and Z − Q − S₂ = ∂R₂ at ω (congrArg) therefore gives Y(ω) − Q(ω) − S₁(ω) = R₁(dω) and Z(ω) − Q(ω) − S₂(ω) = R₂(dω).
3. (The identity.) For the same ω, (Y − Z − S)(ω) = Y(ω) − Z(ω) − (S₁(ω) − S₂(ω)), and ∂R(ω) = R(dω) = R₁(dω) − R₂(dω). Subtracting the two equalities of step 2 gives R₁(dω) − R₂(dω) = (Y(ω) − Q(ω) − S₁(ω)) − (Z(ω) − Q(ω) − S₂(ω)) = Y(ω) − Z(ω) − (S₁(ω) − S₂(ω)), since the Q(ω) terms cancel (linear arithmetic over ℝ). Hence (Y − Z − S)(ω) = ∂R(ω) for every ω, and Y − Z − S = ∂R by extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
4. (The mass bound.) Total mass is M(T) = T.mass = T.massOn U. Apply the sibling lemma cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le (M_G(A − B) ≤ M_G(A) + M_G(B)) with G = U. This gives M(R) = M(R₁ − R₂) ≤ M(R₁) + M(R₂), with A = R₁, B = R₂ in degree m + 2, and M(S) = M(S₁ − S₂) ≤ M(S₁) + M(S₂), with A = S₁, B = S₂ in degree m + 1. Adding (add_le_add) gives M(R) + M(S) ≤ (M(R₁) + M(R₂)) + (M(S₁) + M(S₂)). The right side equals (M(R₁) + M(S₁)) + (M(R₂) + M(S₂)) by commutativity and associativity of addition in [0, ∞] (add_add_add_comm).
5. So R and S are integer multiplicity (step 1), Y − Z − S = ∂R (step 3) and M(R) + M(S) ≤ (M(R₁) + M(S₁)) + (M(R₂) + M(S₂)) (step 4), as claimed. ∎
proof_key_steps: Take R := R₁ − R₂ and S := S₁ − S₂; both are integer multiplicity by (IS), since U is open.
Evaluate both hypotheses at a test form ω, using (A − B)(ω) = A(ω) − B(ω) and ∂T(ω) = T(dω).
Subtract them: Q cancels, giving (Y − Z − S)(ω) = R(dω) = ∂R(ω); conclude by GeometricCurrentOn.ext.
Mass bound from cmc_fc_cs_massOn_sub_le with G = U for R and for S, then add_le_add and add_add_add_comm.

subproblems.title: Diagonal extraction from nested infinite cliques
subproblems.statement: Let C : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop be any family of binary relations C r on ℕ. Suppose that for every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite set I ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite set J ⊆ I such that C r j l holds for all j, l ∈ J. Then there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)) holds for every r ∈ ℕ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (C : ℕ → ℕ → ℕ → Prop), (∀ (r : ℕ) (I : Set ℕ), I.Infinite → ∃ J ⊆ I, J.Infinite ∧ ∀ j ∈ J, ∀ l ∈ J, C r j l) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ ∀ r, C r (φ (r + 1)) (φ r)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 4–5 (nested index sets and diagonal choice) of the parent-supplied proof of cmc_fc_cauchy_subseq, i.e. Simon Ch. 6, proof of 7.2: "apply (1) with ε = 1, 1/2, 1/4 etc. to extract a subsequence {T_{j_r}} … d(T_{j_{r+1}}, T_{j_r}) < 2^{−r}". Here the relation "j and l are 2^{−r}-close" is replaced by an arbitrary relation C r j l.
1. (Choice of refinements.) By the hypothesis and the axiom of choice there is a function F that assigns to each r ∈ ℕ and each infinite I ⊆ ℕ an infinite set F(r, I) ⊆ I such that C r j l for all j, l ∈ F(r, I). Formally, F is a function on the subtype {I : Set ℕ // I.Infinite} with values in the same subtype, obtained by `choose` from the hypothesis.
2. (Nested index sets.) Define I_0 := ℕ (the set univ, which is infinite) and, by recursion on r, I_{r+1} := F(r, I_r). Since F returns infinite sets, every I_r is infinite and the recursion is well defined. By step 1, I_{r+1} ⊆ I_r and C r j l holds for all j, l ∈ I_{r+1}.
3. (Unboundedness.) An infinite set of natural numbers is not bounded above: for every r and every a ∈ ℕ there is b ∈ I_{r+1} with a < b (Set.Infinite.exists_gt). Choose such a b =: g(r, a) for every r and a.
4. (Diagonal choice.) Define φ by recursion: φ(0) := g(0, 0) ∈ I_1 and φ(r + 1) := g(r + 1, φ(r)) ∈ I_{r+2}. Then φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1} for every r, by the choice of g (case r = 0 and case r + 1). Also φ(r) < φ(r + 1) = g(r + 1, φ(r)) for every r. Hence φ is strictly increasing (strictMono_nat_of_lt_succ).
5. (Consecutive terms are related.) Fix r. By step 4, φ(r) ∈ I_{r+1} and φ(r + 1) ∈ I_{r+2}; by step 2, I_{r+2} ⊆ I_{r+1}, so φ(r + 1) ∈ I_{r+1}. Since I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r), step 1 applied to j = φ(r + 1) and l = φ(r) gives C r (φ(r + 1)) (φ(r)). Together with the strict monotonicity of step 4, this proves the claim. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose a refinement F(r, I) ⊆ I: infinite, with all pairs in relation C r.
Nested sets: I_0 = ℕ and I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r); all infinite, decreasing, I_{r+1} pairwise C r.
Diagonal choice: φ(r+1) ∈ I_{r+2} with φ(r+1) > φ(r) (Set.Infinite.exists_gt); φ is StrictMono.
φ(r), φ(r+1) ∈ I_{r+1} = F(r, I_r) gives C r (φ(r+1)) (φ(r)).
